metadata.title: When External Knowledge Should Abstain: Risk-Controlled Evidence Projection for Causal Orientation
metadata.description:
Background knowledge can orient an observational graph, but a confident expert or database can still be wrong. This preprint introduces risk-controlled evidence projection (RCEP), a fail-closed interface with separate source-risk and structural-write contracts. A source is admitted only when a held-out proposal gate certifies its accepted error; admitted proposals may reorient only data-supported pairs, and a total-order projection guarantees acyclicity.

In synthetic corruption experiments, RCEP improves directed F1 by a mean paired gain of 0.096 in informative-confidence conditions; across all 24 conditions, the mean paired gain is 0.053 and the worst-condition gain is 0. The release includes reproducible implementation code, editable vector figures, locked result artifacts, input provenance, and tests. The controlled estimands are accepted-proposal error and deterministic structural invariants under the stated calibration assumptions.

This is a preprint and has not undergone peer review.
metadata.notes: The release does not redistribute third-party raw benchmark inputs. See DATA_AVAILABILITY.md and REPRODUCE.md. The paper-specific companion implementation is maintained at https://github.com/FinalSunFlower/mental-health-system/tree/rcep-preprint.
